title: Representations
gateItems: every Chevalley-Serre relation checks in the tool for every listed representation
acceptance of T12 as automated tests; no-JavaScript run, axe, sizes; reference hashes unchanged

P5-A1.title: Engine phase 5: sparse matrices, minuscule representations, Chevalley-Serre checks, strings
P5-A1.summary: SparseMatrix operations over bigint, minusculeMatrices with the basis in decreasing lexicographic order and the cap, signedMoves, chevalleySerre returning both sides of every relation, stringThrough; the minuscule_representations golden tests.
deliverables: SparseMatrix as Map<'row,column', bigint> with multiply, add, commutator, scale, equality

minusculeMatrices(board, i, cap): the orbit of omega_i (null above cap), basis in decreasing lexicographic order of positions, H_k diagonal by mu_k, F_k sending mu to R_k mu when mu_k = 1, E_k when mu_k = -1, the move matrices E_k + F_k + P_k^0
signedMoves E_k - F_k + P_k^0; chevalleySerre returning a RelationCheck for every relation (hh, he, hf, ef, serre-e, serre-f) with both sides
stringThrough(board, mu, i): mu, mu - alpha_i, ..., mu - mu_i alpha_i by subtracting column i of C

golden tests: for all 18 records the dimension equals the orbit size, the weights equal weights_dynkin_labels where present, and every relation holds; for node 2 of D4 some relation fails and some number in the orbit is 2
acceptance: the 56 of E7 builds in under two seconds
traps: For a node that is not minuscule the recipe fails (D4 omega_2); the tool must show the failure, so chevalleySerre returns both sides rather than throwing.
The basis order is the oracle's: decreasing lexicographic order of the positions (E-5).
Moves in the representation use the firing R_k on positions (weights), not mutations.

P5-A2.title: Tool T12 Representation Builder and MatrixView
P5-A2.summary: For any node of a named board: the orbit drawn in layers with edges coloured by node; the matrices E_k, F_k, H_k as grids up to dimension 27 and as lists above; the relation checker; the move matrix beside its signed version; the string viewer; the failure explanation for non-minuscule nodes; every acceptance criterion of SPEC 4 T12 as tests.
spec: 7.3 (MatrixView as an HTML table with caption and headers)
deliverables: the five features of SPEC 4 T12; matrices built only when the orbit has at most 2000 positions, else the explanation alone; grids up to 27, lists above; the relation checker displaying both sides (MatrixView) and the verdict; the string viewer accepting any position
MatrixView.svelte: an HTML table with caption, row and column headers, sparse display option

T12.test.ts: dimensions equal minuscule_representations[*].dimension; every relation checks for every listed representation; node 2 of D4 shows a failing relation and the explanation that some number in the orbit is 2

T12.spec.ts: A2 node 1 relation checker [E1,F1] = H1 and [E1,F2] = 0; the string viewer on A2 for (2,0) at node 1 shows three positions with the middle one outside the orbit; E7 node 7 loads 56 as a list
acceptance: every bullet of SPEC 4 T12 acceptance has a passing test (G5)
the E7 56 computation runs in the worker or at build time, never as a long task on the main thread (E-9 rule 1: minusculeMatrices is an enumeration)
traps: minusculeMatrices is listed in E-9 as an enumeration: above 2000 expected items it goes to the worker; the orbit sizes are known from orbitSize beforehand.
